| ἦ, καὶ ὑπόδρα ἰδὼν προσεφώνεεν Ἕκτορα δῖον (20.428, whole-line speech introduction, closing the speech before it) | "He spoke, and with a scowl looking at him addressed Hector the heavenly:" | "So he said, and looking at heavenly Hector with a scowl, spoke to him:" | "answered" (reserved for ἀμείβομαι); follows the table’s ἦ καί "He spoke, and" / "So he said, and", ὑπόδρα ἰδών "with a scowl looking" and προσεφώνεεν "addressed" |
| ἦ ῥα, καί (20.438; ἦ "he said", ῥα the particle) | "He spoke, and" | "So he said, and" | "So he spoke, and" (the published English of these words, iliad-019, -029, -043, -067, -113, and the table’s ἦ καί row), "So saying", "With that"; ῥα left untranslated as there |
| γλυκύθυμος · ἀγανόφρων (οὐ γάρ τι γλυκύθυμος ἀνὴρ ἦν οὐδ’ ἀγανόφρων, 20.467) | "sweet-hearted" · "gentle-minded" | "of tender heart" · "of gentle mind" | "kind-hearted", "soft-hearted", "mild" (each flattens one of the two compound halves); γλυκύς "sweet" + θυμός "heart", ἀγανός "gentle" + φρήν "mind" |
| ἐμμεμαώς · μενεαίνων (ἐμμεμαὼς … μενεαίνων, 20.442) | "eager" · "full of eagerness" | "in his eagerness" (said once in `i`) | "raging", "furious" (turned down for μενεαίνω at 4.32, 16.491); ἐμμεμαώς "eager" as μεμαώς (4.73) |
| νύσσω (νύξ’, 20.489) | "stabbed" | "stabbed" | "pricked", "jabbed", "pierced" (πείρω, πέρησε), "wounded" (reserved for οὐτάω in `l`); follows the table’s νύξ’ (5.46), which fixes "stabbed" in both layers |
| ἐλαύνω of a sword-stroke (ξίφει ἤλασε, 20.475) | "struck" | "struck" | "drove" (the table reserves it for the chariot-driving ἐλαύνω); the sword is the instrument in the dative, so the verb is "struck" |
| κλονέων · εἰλυφάζει (πάντῃ τε κλονέων ἄνεμος φλόγα εἰλυφάζει, 20.492) | "throwing into confusion" · "swirls" | "throwing it into confusion on every side" · "swirls … about" (+ note: εἰλυφάζει rare, sense from the context) | "buffeting", "tossing", "driving" (each picks a picture; the table has "throwing … into confusion" for κλονέω in both layers, 4.302, 5.96), "whirls" (turned down for the related εἰλυφόων, 11.156, which has "swirling") |
| ἀναμαιμάει (βαθέ’ ἄγκεα … πῦρ, 20.490; rare verb, meaning not known) | "rages through" | "rages through" (+ note: exact sense not known) | "sweeps through", "ravages", "burns" (each decides the sense); ἄγκεα "glens" |
| τριβέμεναι κρῖ λευκόν (20.496) | "to rub … white barley" | "to thresh white barley" | "to grind", "to tread out", "to crush"; τρίβω "rub", κρῖ λευκόν "white barley" (5.196) |
| ῥίμφα … λέπτ’ ἐγένοντο (20.497) | "lightly it becomes fine" | "lightly it is made fine" | "swiftly" (reserved for θοός, ὠκύς), "quickly", "nimbly" (8.54); ῥίμφα "lightly" as in the table’s 6.511 |
| ἐϋκτιμένῃ ἐν ἀλωῇ (20.496) | "on a well-built threshing-floor" | "on a well-built threshing-floor" | "well-tilled" (the Odyssey’s ἐϋκτιμένη ἀλωή is a garden plot, 24.226), "well-founded"; ἀλωή "threshing-floor" as in the table’s ἀλωάς (5.499) |
| ἐριμύκων (βοῶν ὑπὸ πόσσ’ ἐριμύκων, 20.497) | "loud-bellowing" | "loud-bellowing" | "deep-lowing", "much-bellowing"; ἐρι- "very" + μυκάομαι "bellow" |
| Ἀρηΐθοον θεράποντα (Ἀρηΐθοον θεράποντα, 20.487; apposition) | "Areithous, the attendant" | "Areithous, his attendant" | "servant" (reserved for δμῶς); θεράπων "attendant" (2.110) |
| Names (20.419–503) | Polydorus · Dryops · Demuchus · Philetor · Laogonus · Dardanus · Bias · Tros · Alastor · Mulius · Agenor · Echeclus · Deucalion · Peirous · Rhigmus · Thrace · Areithous | same | "Peiros" and "Peires" for Πείρεω (the genitive of Πείρως, "Peirous" in iliad-015, -026), "Rigmus" (every Ῥ- name is "Rh-": Rhesus, Rhexenor), "Moulios"; Latinised like the other Greek names |
| Departures from odyssey-010 (νήπιος, οὐδὲ τὸ ᾔδη ὃ οὐ πείσεσθαι ἔμελλεν, 20.466, the line of odyssey-010) | `l` "foolish, nor did he know this, that he was not to be won over" | `i` "foolish as he was, he did not know that Achilles was not to be won over" | the Odyssey’s `l` "fool … that he was not to persuade her" and `i` "the fool, for he did not know that she was not to be won over". Three departures: νήπιος is "foolish" / "foolish as he was" by the Iliad table (2.38, 5.406, 16.46), not "fool"; πείσεσθαι is the future middle of πείθομαι "be persuaded", so `l` is made passive; `i` names Achilles because with Tros the only "he" the reader would take him to be the one not won over |
